# NGAP: compliance register

What this is: the requirements of this area that are built and verified against running code, the typed rows recorded while building them, and coverage counts derived from the specs (verification.md §5). Requirements are in [`requirements.md`](../../requirements.md); deviations in [`deviations.md`](../deviations.md).

Specs read: TS 38.413 j40.

Row suffixes (requirements.md): -D defect in the sim, -B a choice the spec leaves open, -G declared gap, -V deviation from a "shall", -S spec contradiction and the reading chosen, -M mutant, -T T0 reading or measurement, -F a kaluza-core defect the sim found, -X retired. Verification: U unit, KAT or oracle test; F fuzz or property test; I interop; L lab; G gate row; A real-device comparison.

| KS-NGAP-B1 | 2026-10-15 | NGAP and F1AP builders and readers as built in P1 N7 (src/codec/asn1/msg/{ngap,f1ap}), the RRC route (KS-RRC-B2): a typed struct per message of the P1 sets (ADR 0009 point h without sessions; F1 Setup, the RRC message transfers, UE Context Setup, Modification, Release Request and Release, Paging, Error Indication), inputs checked, built as JER, encoded strictly as APER by the generated code; readers decode APER and read the IEs P1 interprets; peek() reads the procedure, class, criticality and UE IDs of any PDU for the TS 38.413 10 handling. The CU-CP copies it into SecretBytes as soon as the request is read and wipes the codec's octets; the JER helpers overwrite every string of a value (the JER text built or read included) before freeing it. asn1c frees its own decode buffers without wiping them.
